prompt: Some people think that team sports prepare children for work life but others think individual sports are better. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that team sports such as football and basketball give children the skills they need for their future careers, while others believe that individual sports like swimming or tennis are more beneficial. In my opinion, both types bring valuable lessons, but team sports offer better preparation for working life.

On the one hand, individual sports teach children how to depend on themselves. An athlete who trains alone must manage his own time, set personal goals and stay motivated without support from teammates. These habits are clearly useful in the workplace, where employees are often judged by their personal results. For example, a young swimmer learns discipline by waking up early every morning to practice, and this discipline can help him succeed in any job.

On the other hand, team sports develop social skills that are difficult to learn alone. Children who play in a team must communicate with others, share responsibility and accept different roles. Sometimes they must also deal with conflicts between players, which is similar to solving problems with colleagues in a company. Moreover, modern companies value cooperation more than ever, because most projects are completed by groups rather than individuals.

In conclusion, although individual sports build self-reliance and discipline, I believe team sports prepare children better for their professional life because almost every job requires working with other people. Parents should encourage their children to try both kinds of sports, but they should not forget that the ability to cooperate is one of the most important skills in the modern world.
